title: Christmas weekend
topic: A four-day weekend that counts a public holiday and the weekend as PTO winnings
blurb: A friend is proud of turning one Friday off into four vacation days.
prompt: A friend just texted this in the group chat. If one line doesn't add up, tap it.

segments.label: The calendar
segments.text: Christmas is on a Thursday this year, so the office is already closed that day.

segments.label: The Friday
segments.text: If I take Friday off, I get Thursday through Sunday at home.

segments.label: The flex
segments.text: So one PTO day turns into four full days off — I'm basically getting four days of vacation for the price of one.

segments.label: The booking
segments.text: I'll book the Friday morning train before the tickets jump.

conclusion: One Friday of PTO buys a four-day vacation, because Thursday through Sunday are all off.

flaws.original: I'll have a four-day stretch at home, but Thursday was already a holiday and the weekend was already mine. The one PTO day only adds Friday.
flaws.corrupted: So one PTO day turns into four full days off — I'm basically getting four days of vacation for the price of one.

diagnosis_choices.label: Thursday was already a holiday, and Saturday and Sunday were already yours. One PTO day only buys Friday.
Taking Friday off doesn't connect to Sunday, because Saturday is a working day this year.
Christmas falling on a Thursday means the office is also closed on Friday, so the PTO is wasted.
A train on Friday morning uses up part of the day, so it isn't four full days at home.

fix_choices.label: Call it a four-day weekend if you want, but admit only Friday is the extra day you paid for.
Also take Monday off, so the four paid days finally match the four days at home.
Move the PTO to Thursday, since Christmas might not count as a real holiday.
Book the train on Thursday instead, which turns the holiday into a work-travel day and evens it out.

flaws.explanation: Saturday and Sunday were already yours — and so was Christmas. One PTO day only buys Friday.
flaws.why_tempting: A four-day stretch feels like a prize, so people count the whole cluster as something the PTO created.
flaws.catch_rule: When someone turns a short leave into a long 'vacation,' subtract the weekend and the holiday you already had.
flaws.hint: Which of those four days would you have had off even without filing any PTO?

practice.problem: New Year's Day is a Wednesday. A friend takes Thursday and Friday off and says, 'Three PTO days? No — I just turned two days into a five-day vacation.' What's the catch?
practice.answer: Wednesday was already a holiday, and the weekend was already off. The two PTO days only add Thursday and Friday.

clean_segments: Christmas is on a Thursday this year, so the office is already closed that day.
If I take Friday off, I get Thursday through Sunday at home.
I'll have a four-day stretch at home, but Thursday was already a holiday and the weekend was already mine. The one PTO day only adds Friday.
I'll book the Friday morning train before the tickets jump.
clean_conclusion: It's a four-day weekend, but only Friday is the extra day the PTO bought.
